title: 3.4 Aspects of Morality: Religious Morality & Nature 🌿
content: 📌 እንኳን ወደዚህ የትምህርት ክፍለ-ጊዜ በሰላም መጡ! 👋 የትምህርት ጊዜዎ ስኬታማ እና ፍሬያማ እንዲሆን መልካም ምኞቴን እገልጻለሁ። ይህ የምዕራፍ 3 ሁለተኛው ክፍል (Chapter 3 Part 2) ሲሆን፣ ትምህርቱን በጥንቃቄ እንዲከታተሉ በአክብሮት እጋብዛለሁ።👇👇 Four Aspects of Morality: 1. Religious Morality 2. Morality and Nature 3. Individual Morality 4. Social Morality 1. Religious Morality (Human to Supernatural): • Refers to a human being in relationship to a supernatural being/God. • Example: The first 3 of the Ten Commandments (e.g., "Do not worship false gods", "Keep holy the Sabbath") govern a person's relationship with God alone. • Violating these harms one's relationship with God without necessarily harming other humans. 2. Morality and Nature (Human to Nature): • Refers to human actions toward the environment and natural world. • Common in Native American, Far East cultures, and modern Western ethics. • Nature can be viewed as having intrinsic value (valuable in itself) rather than just instrumental value for humans. • Desert Island Example: Robinson Crusoe living alone can still act morally or immorally based on how he treats nature. 👉 ስነ-ምግባር በ 4 አበይት ክፍሎች ይከፈላል። የመጀመሪያው ሃይማኖታዊ ስነ-ምግባር ሲሆን የሰው ልጅ ከፈጣሪው ጋር ያለውን ግንኙነት ይመለከታል (ለምሳሌ የመጀመሪያዎቹ 10ቱ ትእዛዛት)። ሁለተኛው ተፈጥሮአዊ ስነ-ምግባር ሲሆን የሰው ልጅ ከተፈጥሮ ጋር ያለውን ግንኙነት ያሳያል። ተፈጥሮ በራሷ ውድ እሴት ስላላት አንድ ሰው ብቻውን በምድረ-በዳ ቢኖር እንኳ ተፈጥሮን በመንከባከብ ወይም በመጉዳት የሞራል/ኢ-ሞራላዊ ድርጊት ሊፈጽም ይችላል። 💡 Exam Hint: Note the difference: Violating the first 3 commandments is an offense in Religious Morality, while treating nature with respect is Natural Morality!

title: 3.4.3 Individual Morality & 3.4.4 Social Morality 👥
content: 📌 3. Individual Morality (Human to Self): • Refers to individuals in relation to themselves and their personal inner conscience. • Represents a "higher morality" coming from within, regardless of whether society, law, or religion demands it. • A person acts right simply because their conscience tells them it is right. 4. Social Morality (Human to Other Humans): • Concerns human beings in relation to other human beings. • Most Important Aspect: Cuts across all other aspects and exists in almost every ethical system. • Desert Island Comparison: Robinson Crusoe's moral potential expands vastly if 9 other people join the island—actions like subjugating, torturing, or destroying others create profound social moral consequences. 👉 ግለሰባዊ ስነ-ምግባር (Individual Morality): ሰው ከራሱ ህሊና ጋር ያለው ግንኙነት ሲሆን፣ ህጉ ወይም ሃይማኖቱ ስላለ ሳይሆን ህሊናው ትክክል ነው ብሎ ስላመነበት ብቻ የሚያደርገው ነው። ማህበራዊ ስነ-ምግባር (Social Morality): ከሌሎች ሰዎች ጋር ያለንን ግንኙነት የሚመለከትና በሁሉም የኢቲክስ አስተምህሮዎች ውስጥ የሚገኝ በጣም ዋናው ክፍል ነው። 💡 Exam Focus: Social Morality is considered the most pervasive and vital aspect of ethics because it directly governs interpersonal conflict and cooperation!

title: 3.5 Who is Morally / Ethically Responsible? 🐺
content: 📌 Humans as Sole Moral Agents: • Morality applies only to human beings; holding animals or plants morally responsible ignores scientific evidence of instinctual behavior. Are Animals Morally Responsible? • Currently, animals and plants are classified as non-moral or amoral (lacking a moral sense or being completely outside the moral sphere). • Wolf vs. Sheep Example: If a wolf kills a sheep, we do not hold the wolf morally responsible or judge it as "evil". We may kill the wolf to protect livestock, not to punish it morally. • If future science proves animals can develop complex rational/thought processes, they might be taught morality and held responsible. 👉 ስነ-ምግባራዊ ተጠያቂነት የሰው ልጅ ብቻ መገለጫ ነው። እንስሳትና እፅዋት በኢንስቲንክት (የተፈጥሮ ስሜት) ስለሚመሩ Non-moral ወይም Amoral ይባላሉ። ለምሳሌ ተኩላ በግ ቢበላ ሞራላዊ ወንጀለኛ አይደለም፤ ተኩላውን የምንገድለው ለጥንቃቄ እንጂ የሞራል ቅጣት ለመስጠት አይደለም። 💡 Exam Hint: Differentiate between immoral (human doing bad) and non-moral/amoral (entities like animals or objects outside the moral sphere)!

title: 3.5.1 Moral Judgments & Voluntary Actions ⚖️
content: 📌 Nature of Moral Judgments: • Moral judgments decide what is right/wrong or good/bad in human relations. • Voluntary vs. Involuntary Actions: - Applies ONLY to voluntary actions (freely chosen choices). - Involuntary actions (out of human control) are rarely subject to moral judgment. Key Characteristics: • Evaluative: Places value on actions, relations, and choices. • Normative: Assesses the moral worth of actions based on standards or norms. Onora O’Neill’s Insight: • Moral principles are not an "auto-pilot for life." • Applying rules requires personal judgment, sensitivity, discernment, intelligence, and goodwill. 👉 የሞራል ፍርድ (Moral Judgment) የሚሰጠው በሰው ልጅ በፈቃደኝነት በሚከናወኑ (Voluntary) ድርጊቶች ላይ ብቻ ነው። ከአቅም በላይ ወይም ያለ ፈቃድ የተደረጉ (Involuntary) ድርጊቶች በሞራል አያስጠይቁም። የሞራል ህጎች እንደ አውቶፓይለት አውቶማቲክ አይደሉም፤ አስተዋይነትና ቅንነትን ይፈልጋሉ። 💡 Exam Focus: Remember the two key qualities of moral judgments: Evaluative (assigning value) and Normative (measuring against norms)!

title: Evaluating Conduct: Motives and Means 🎯
content: 📌 When judging moral conduct, 4 factors must be evaluated: Motives, Means, Consequences, and the Situation. 1. Motives (Intention - Why an action is done): • Basic foundation of morality (Jesus, Kant). • Good motive is essential for unqualified approval. If unforeseen bad consequences occur, a good motive softens blame ("he meant well"). • Kant's "Good Will": Nothing is good without qualification except a good will. True moral acts are done out of pure duty to moral law, not inclination or self-interest. 2. Means (Instruments/Methods used): • The method used to achieve an end. • We condemn actions if unjust or cruel means are used, even for a good goal. • Warning: "The end justifies the means" is dangerous because chosen means become part of the act's total effect. 👉 ሞቲቭ (Motive): ድርጊቱን ለማድረግ ያነሳሳን አላማ ነው። ካንት እንደሚለው እውነተኛ መልካም ነገር "መልካም ፈቃድ (Good Will)" ብቻ ነው። ሚንስ (Means): ግቡን ለማሳካት የተጠቀምንበት መንገድ ሲሆን፣ "አላማው መንገዱን ያጸድቀዋል" ብሎ ጨካኝ መንገድ መጠቀም ተቀባይነት የለውም። 💡 Exam Hint: For Kant, moral worth rests in the individual's will acting purely out of duty.

title: Evaluating Conduct: Consequences & Moral Situation 🌐
content: 📌 3. Consequences (Results/Effects): • The final outcome of a moral decision. • We expect right actions to yield good consequences. • Contrast: Kant focuses on good motives; Utilitarians focus on good consequences/results. • Ideal Judgment: Society judges conduct as completely "right" when it stems from a good motive + uses just means + produces good consequences. 4. The Moral Situation: • Involves Moral Agents—human beings who act, hold rights/duties, and make conscious choices between moral alternatives. 👉 ኮንሴክዌንስ (Consequences): የድርጊቱ የመጨረሻ ውጤት ነው። ካንት ትኩረቱ ነባሩ አላማ (Motive) ላይ ሲሆን፣ ዩቲሊቴሪያኖች ግን ትኩረታቸው ውጤቱ (Consequences) ላይ ነው። ሙሉ በሙሉ ትክክለኛ ድርጊት የሚባለው፦ ጥሩ አላማ + ጥሩ መንገድ + ጥሩ ውጤት ሲኖረው ነው። 💡 Exam Focus: Know the philosophical distinction: Kantian Ethics = Motive/Duty vs. Utilitarianism = Consequences/Results!

title: 3.5.2 What Makes an Action Moral? 🧩
content: 📌 Moral vs. Non-Moral Actions: • Non-moral / Morally Neutral: Actions outside moral scope (e.g., putting on a raincoat, sharpening a pencil, standing on your head). • Morally Significant: Actions carrying positive/negative ethical weight (e.g., stealing, punching someone, helping the needy). 3 Core Features of a Moral Act: 1. Involves an Agent: Performed by a creature with free will/choice. 2. Involves Intention: Done deliberately with a motive. (Note: Accidental negligence can still be morally culpable). 3. Affects Others (Moral Patients): Brings significant harm or benefit to other beings. Self-Affecting Behavior Controversy: • Does morality govern acts affecting only oneself (e.g., drug use)? Often viewed through religious lenses rather than strictly pure ethical grounds. 👉 እርሳስ መቁረጥ ወይም የዝናብ ልብስ መልበስ Morally Neutral ሲሆኑ፣ መስረቅ ወይም መረዳት ግን Morally Significant ናቸው። አንድ ድርጊት የሞራል ድርጊት ለመባል 3 ነገሮች ያስፈልጉታል፦ ነፃ ፈቃድ ያለው አድራጊ (Agent)፣ አላማ/ (Intention)፣ እና በሌሎች ላይ የሚያመጣው ተጽእኖ (Affecting others)። 💡 Exam Hint: Memorize the 3 key components of a moral action for multiple choice and short answer questions!

title: 3.6 Why Should Human Beings Be Moral? (Core Arguments) 💡
content: 📌 Why should people do right acts rather than wrong acts? Beyond supernatural/religious reasons, 3 rational arguments exist: 1. Argument from Enlightened Self-Interest: • If everyone avoids killing, stealing, or lying, every individual benefits. • "It is in my self-interest to do good because I benefit, and I avoid being ostracized/punished." (Foundation of Ethical Egoism). 2. Argument from Tradition and Law: • Long-established laws and traditions guide human harmony. Respects human effort spent building stable societies across history. 3. Common Human Needs: • All humans share universal needs: love, peace, safety, freedom, happiness. Moral principles are necessary to cooperate and fulfill these needs without fear. 👉 ሰው ለምን ደግ መሆን አለበት? 3 ዋና ምክንያቶች፦ 1. Enlightened Self-Interest: ሁሉም ሰው ጥሩ ቢሆን የራሳችንም ህይወት ሰላም ይሆናል። 2. Tradition & Law: ለህጎችና ባህሎች ማህበራዊ እሴት ያለን አክብሮት። 3. Common Human Needs: ፍቅር፣ ሰላምና ደስታን ለማግኘት በጋራ የመኖር አስፈላጊነት። 💡 Exam Focus: Enlightened Self-Interest shows that setting aside selfish desires actually serves our long-term interests through mutual benefit!

title: Social Benefits of Morality & Individual Motivation 🤝
content: 📌 Why Society Needs Moral Rules (Thomas Hobbes Perspective): Morality is a social activity that enables collective flourishing. Hobbes outlines 5 Key Social Benefits: 1. Keeps society from falling apart. 2. Reduces human suffering. 3. Promotes human flourishing. 4. Resolves conflicts of interest in just ways. 5. Assigns praise, blame, reward, punishment, and guilt. Why Should *I* Be Moral? • Even when breaking a rule seems unpunished, following moral rules overall creates a stable system that benefits the individual long-term. Common Motivations: • Self-respect, social approval, avoiding punishment, divine faith, or being a role model. 👉 እንደ ቶማስ ሆብስ አመለካከት ሞራል ማህበረሰቡን ከውድቀት ይታደጋል፣ መከራን ይቀንሳል፣ እድገትን ያመጣል፣ ግጭቶችን ይፈታል፣ እና ምስጋናና ቅጣትን በፍትህ ይመድባል። ግለሰቦች የሞራል ስርዓትን መከተል ያለባቸው የረጅም ጊዜ ሰላምና እድገት ለማግኘት ነው። 💡 Exam Hint: Be prepared to list or identify the 5 social benefits of moral rules according to Thomas Hobbes!

title: Chapter Summary: Moral Practice & Character 🎹
content: 📌 Key Chapter Takeaways: • Ethical reasoning structures help us make rational, respectful, and balanced decisions. • Ethical theories serve as guidance tools for moral analysis. Aristotle's Piano Analogy (Virtue Practice): • Developing moral character requires constant moral practice. • Knowing moral rules intellectually is not enough. • Analogy: Just as a pianist cannot play well without practicing regularly (even if she knows the theory), a person cannot be moral without consistently practicing virtue. 👉 የኢቲክስ እውቀት ብቻውን በቂ አይደለም፤ ተግባራዊ ልምምድ ያሻዋል። አርስቶትል እንደሚያስረዳው አንድ የፒያኖ ተጫዋች ንድፈ-ሀሳቡን አውቆ ሳያዘወትር ካልተለማመደ ጥሩ ተጫዋች መሆን እንደማይችል ሁሉ፣ አንድ ሰው የሞራል ህጎችን ስለአወቀ ብቻ መልካም ሰው አይሆንም፤ ሁልጊዜ በግብር መለማመድ አለበት። 💡 Exam Focus: Remember Aristotle’s core teaching: Moral virtue is a habit formed through active, continuous practice! --- 🎯 ❤️ የምዕራፍ 3 ሁለተኛው እና የመጨረሻው ክፍል (Chapter 3 Part 2) በዚህ ተጠናቋል። ይህንን የትምህርት ክፍል በስኬት በማጠናቀቅዎ እንኳን ደስ አለዎት! ለትምህርቱ ያሳዩት ትጋት እና ተሞክሮ ለፈተናዎ ከፍተኛ ውጤት እንደሚደርስ ሙሉ እምነቴ ነው። ለላቀ የስኬት ማዕረግ እንዲደርሱ መልካም የፈተና ጊዜና ብሩህ ተስፋ እመኛለሁ! ምስጋናዬ ከላቀ ምኞት ጋር ይድረስዎት🙏🙏🙏!
